newDescription:
In this L3 11+ Maths lesson, students develop advanced statistics skills by interpreting, comparing and reasoning with bar charts, line graphs and pie charts.

This lesson includes:
✔ Reading bar charts accurately, including axes, scales, categories and titles
✔ Comparing values and finding differences from bar-chart data
✔ Reading and interpreting line graphs to identify increases, decreases and periods of no change
✔ Calculating changes over time by comparing starting and finishing values
✔ Reading pie charts as fractions and percentages of a whole
✔ Using a known total to calculate the number represented by each pie-chart section
✔ Working backwards from a known part to find the whole
✔ Converting between fractions, percentages and quantities
✔ Comparing paired or grouped bar charts
✔ Solving missing-bar problems using multiples, fractions and proportional reasoning
✔ Testing statistical statements and proving whether they are true or false using calculations
✔ Using pie charts to solve multi-step problems involving totals, differences and combined groups

Students begin by revisiting the structure of bar charts, including the x-axis, y-axis, scale and category labels. They practise extracting values and comparing quantities before moving on to line graphs, where they interpret change over time and distinguish between final values and actual increases.

The lesson then develops pie-chart reasoning. Students use fractions and percentages to calculate quantities from a total, work backwards from a known section to find the whole, and solve questions involving equal sectors, combined categories and comparisons.

Later activities require deeper reasoning with grouped bar charts and incomplete data. Students use clues involving multiples, fractions and proportions to determine missing values, then justify answers using clear calculations.

The lesson finishes with multi-step pie-chart challenges in which students evaluate statements, calculate totals and differences, and combine information across several categories.

By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to interpret a range of statistical representations confidently, select appropriate calculations, and justify conclusions from data.
